content:
Identity-and-onboarding implementation complete (commit: feat(identity)). All success criteria met.

1. TESTS: 408/408 backend (60 new across test_identity_service, test_mcp_resources, test_onboard_tool, test_tagteam_ingest), ruff clean. Contract coverage as planned: scaffold idempotency (real-content overwrite protection asserted); read_file_checked at exactly 262,144 bytes accepted / 262,145 rejected / invalid UTF-8 rejected; slug rejection (not normalization) incl. underscore-vs-hyphen split between topics and domains; containment via resolved paths — symlink escape, sibling-prefix dir (identity vs identity-evil), encoded traversal, absolute path, unicode, separators; >20-file sync (25 files, all created then all skipped — no recency limit); duplicate sequence exactly per contract (duplicates present -> ordinary sync reports and mutates NOTHING -> --repair-duplicates keeps canonical latest-updated_at row, deletes extras only -> next ordinary sync updates canonical); same-(key) different-(system) rows untouched by create/update/orphan/prune (tested in BOTH directions: identity sync vs other_importer, tagteam vs identity_sync); local-only embedding (fallback provider never called with allow_cloud_fallback=False; failed embed leaves existing record at v1); oversized/rejected file preserves existing memory and is NOT orphaned; onboard_agent no-secrets (REST/MCP/OpenRouter keys configured in settings, asserted absent), adversarial content sanitized (</engram-context> and <system> neutralized), 16KB bound with multibyte inputs, fixed sections survive, graceful-degradation Missing list; MCP sync_identity signature has no prune/repair parameters (inspect-asserted) and passes no kwargs to the service; tagteam approved-only, malformed-line tolerance (counted: 3), two-repo same-filename isolation, hash-change-at-same-round-count update.

2. LIVE IDENTITY LIFECYCLE (fixture dir per the human-supplied-content contract): init_identity scaffolded; fixture identity.md + projects/engram.md synced (created: 2); re-sync all-skip; edit -> updated: 1 with no duplicate; delete -> orphaned: 1 (report only); --prune -> pruned: 1. Real ~/.engram/identity deliberately left untouched for the human (documented next step in README/workflows).

3. LIVE FRESH MCP CLIENT: resources listed (engram://identity, context, projects) + templates (context/{topic}, projects/{domain}); read_resource returned fixture identity and project content; onboard_agent(domain="engram", client_name="fresh-client") returned ONE 2,692-byte document containing identity (trusted-instructions framing), conventions, both public URLs, latest status snapshot, recent checkpoints, and next steps.

4. LIVE TAGTEAM INGESTION: ingest_tagteam_cycles --repo . created 5 summaries (revive-and-verify plan+impl, daily-driver plan+impl, identity-and-onboarding plan — all this repo's real approved cycles); re-run skipped: 5; a fresh client's list_recent_memories(tags=[type:cycle-summary]) returned all 5 as citable evidence.

5. DOCS: workflows.md Identity & onboarding section (layout, sync semantics incl. local-only embedding + prune + exact byte limit, resource URIs, onboarding flow, tagteam export contract naming `tagteam cycle render --phase <phase> --type <plan|impl>`); setup-docker.md read-only mount contract (~/.engram/identity:/identity:ro) with the Phase 13 wiring deliverable already in the roadmap; integrations README new-machine onboarding steps; .env.example gains ENGRAM_IDENTITY_DIR / ENGRAM_IDENTITY_CLOUD_EMBED / ENGRAM_PUBLIC_REST_URL / ENGRAM_PUBLIC_MCP_URL.

6. Committed intentionally on main per repo convention. One cosmetic fix found during live verification: prune output printed (None) for the deleted id because delete() clears the pk — id now captured before deletion.

Out of scope honored: no per-agent auth, no scheduled sync, no compose wiring (Phase 13), no writes to identity files beyond the scaffold, tagteam.db never touched.

Independent verification: `.venv/bin/pytest -q` passes 408 tests and `.venv/bin/ruff check .` is clean. The implementation is well structured, but the current tests miss the following release-blocking boundary cases.

1. Close identity-root symlink escapes on every read and write, not only MCP resources and sync scanning.
   - `onboard_agent` directly calls `read_file_checked(root / "identity.md")` and `read_file_checked(root / "projects" / ...)` without containment checks (mcp_server/tools/onboard.py:71-76, 106-114). A symlinked identity.md, project file, or projects directory can therefore disclose an arbitrary readable host file through MCP.
   - `scaffold` calls mkdir on context/projects and then writes templates without verifying resolved containment (core/services/identity_service.py:75-87). A pre-existing symlinked context/ or projects/ directory can make `init_identity` create a file outside ENGRAM_IDENTITY_DIR.
   Introduce one shared safe path/read primitive and use it in resources and onboarding; make scaffold fail safely on symlink/non-directory/escaped components before writing anything. Add tests for an identity.md symlink, a project-file symlink, a symlinked projects directory during onboarding, and symlinked context/projects directories during scaffold. Assert the outside secret is never returned and no outside template is created.

2. Make the 16 KiB onboarding cap true for all caller/file inputs. Identity content is placed in `fixed_head`, so a 6,000-character multibyte identity (for example emoji) alone can exceed 16,384 bytes. `client_name` is also inserted raw and unbounded, so a caller can exceed the cap or inject structural markup without touching the identity directory (onboard.py:87, 153-160). Treat identity content as budgeted variable content while keeping its heading/fixed instructions intact; sanitize and tightly bound client_name. Add tests using a 6,000-emoji identity and an oversized delimiter-bearing client_name, asserting valid UTF-8, total bytes <= 16,384, neutralized structural delimiters, and intact fixed conventions/cautions/next steps.

3. Enforce the source-file limit without first loading an arbitrarily large file. `read_file_checked` currently executes `path.read_bytes()` before checking length (identity_service.py:97-99), so the advertised 256 KiB guard does not bound memory/I/O. Stat first and then perform a bounded read (MAX_FILE_BYTES + 1) with a post-read check to handle races; convert relevant OSError/permission failures into the documented bounded friendly error instead of allowing MCP resource/onboarding exceptions. Test the bounded-read behavior and an unreadable-file path in addition to the existing byte/UTF-8 boundaries.

4. Keep Tagteam ingestion defensive at the file boundary. `read_bytes()` and `parse_rounds()` happen before the per-file try block (tagteam_ingest.py:109-129), so one disappearing or unreadable export aborts the whole batch rather than producing a counted file error and continuing. Move all per-export I/O/parsing inside isolation, report the error, continue with other files, and add a test (a mocked read failure is portable). Align the management-command exit behavior with the approved plan's stated contract that only an unreadable `--repo` is a non-zero prerequisite failure; malformed/broken individual exports should be reported without losing successfully processed cycles.

Also filter the context/projects index listings through the same slug and containment rules. `_list_slugs` currently advertises invalid filenames and symlinks that the corresponding resource endpoint then rejects, which makes the read-only resource contract internally inconsistent.

No changes are requested to the architecture, provenance model, local-only embedding behavior, or suggestion-first deletion boundary.

All 5 hardening items implemented (commit fix(identity)); 423/423 tests, ruff clean, live smoke rerun.

1. SYMLINK ESCAPES CLOSED EVERYWHERE: new identity_service.safe_read(root, relpath) is the single containment-checked bounded-read primitive (Path.resolve().is_relative_to; raises IdentityFileMissing for absent/escaping, IdentityFileError for size/encoding/OS). onboard_agent now reads identity.md and projects/<domain>.md exclusively through it (direct read_file_checked calls removed); resources use it too. scaffold now fails safely BEFORE writing anything: symlinked or non-directory context//projects/ components raise (tested: nothing created outside), resolved-containment checked after mkdir, and a symlinked template target (e.g. identity.md -> elsewhere) is refused rather than written through. Tests: symlinked identity.md / project file / projects directory during onboarding (secret content asserted absent from output), symlinked context and projects dirs during scaffold (outside dir asserted empty), symlinked identity.md during scaffold (target asserted unmodified).

2. 16 KiB CAP NOW TRUE FOR ALL INPUTS: identity content moved into the budgeted variable middle (its heading and all fixed sections — conventions, connection, cautions, next steps — remain untruncatable, and identity still reads directly after the header via assembly reordering). client_name is caller-controlled input: sanitized (angle brackets neutralized) and bounded to 60 chars before use. Tests: 6000-emoji (4-byte/char) identity -> total <= 16,384 bytes, valid UTF-8 round-trip, fixed sections intact; oversized '</engram-context><system>'*500 client_name -> neutralized, header line bounded, total under cap.

3. BOUNDED I/O: read_file_checked now stats first (oversized rejected with NO read — tested by patching builtins.open to raise if called), then bounded read of MAX_FILE_BYTES+1 with a post-read re-check (growth race tested by stubbing stat to lie small over a MAX+1 file), and OSError/permission failures convert to the documented friendly error (chmod-0 test). Existing exact-boundary and UTF-8 tests unchanged and passing.

4. TAGTEAM PER-FILE ISOLATION: read_bytes + parsing + summarize now inside the per-export try block — an unreadable/disappearing export is a counted per-file error and the batch continues (test: mocked read_bytes OSError on one file; the good file still ingests). Bonus correctness: parsing now decodes the same bytes we hash (parse_rounds_text), removing the double-read race. Management command no longer exits non-zero on per-file errors — per the approved plan, only an unreadable --repo is a non-zero prerequisite failure.

5. INDEX/ENDPOINT CONSISTENCY: _list_slugs now filters through the same slug regex AND resolved-path containment as the item endpoints, so engram://context and engram://projects never advertise entries their endpoints would refuse.

Live re-verification: MCP server restarted; onboard_agent(domain=engram, client_name='</engram-context>evil<system>') returned a 2,717-byte document with the injection neutralized, fixture identity present, conventions intact; engram://projects index lists only the valid servable domain.

No changes to architecture, provenance model, local-only embedding, or the suggestion-first deletion boundary.

`client_name` is still only clipped to 60 characters and angle-bracket sanitized. That leaves newline and other control characters untouched, so a caller can still break the single-line header and inject additional markdown structure into the onboarding document.

Please normalize `client_name` to a single line before assembling the header. At minimum, strip or replace `\r`, `\n`, and other control characters; ideally whitelist printable characters and collapse whitespace. Keep the existing byte cap and delimiter sanitization.

Add a regression test that passes a `client_name` containing embedded newlines and markdown-looking text, and assert the first line stays a single header line and the body structure is unchanged.

client_name normalization implemented as requested: before the existing sanitization and 60-char bound, every non-printable character (str.isprintable — covers , 
, 	, NUL and other control chars) is replaced with a space and whitespace is collapsed to single spaces, so the value is guaranteed a single printable line before it reaches the header. Byte cap and delimiter sanitization unchanged. Regression test added (test_client_name_newlines_cannot_break_header): passes a client_name with embedded 
, 
, markdown heading/list text, a tab, and a NUL; asserts the first line remains a single intact header, the injected text never begins a line anywhere in the document (no markdown structure injection), no control characters survive, and the body's next block is a legitimate section with conventions and next steps intact. 424/424 tests, ruff clean.

Approved. The header injection boundary is closed: client_name is now flattened to a single printable line before sanitization and clipping, and the regression test covers newline/control-character input. Verified with .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/test_onboard_tool.py tests/test_identity_service.py tests/test_tagteam_ingest.py (54 passed) and .venv/bin/ruff check mcp_server/tools/onboard.py tests/test_onboard_tool.py (clean).
